name: Magma viewing chamber
purpose: The hush zone at the bottom of the spa: guests sit in silence on long benches in front of a wall of thick glass with a slow lava sea beyond, and feel the mountain's own rumble.

ceiling_profile.note: Low flat basalt vault with timber beams over each glass bay; lowest at the north wall.

hero.why: An 82 m wall of thick glass in bronze-framed bays with lava moving slowly beyond (23, 36): the only reason for the room, and by far its brightest light.

anchored.why: Timber floor along the glass (36); rock floor behind it.
Long low bench facing the glass, centred on a bay; benches alternate with empty bays so the floor stays open.

sightlines.see: The whole glass wall opening up to the left and right, orange.
Back west: the tunnel mouth's amber lanterns, the way out.

concept.match: Square-on to the glass: repeated bronze-framed bays, lava filling every pane, a row of silhouettes along the rail, low timber ceiling beams, dark floor reflecting orange (B4 strip of 23).

lights.note: Lava light is the key light; everything else is a dim accent.

lights.why: Tiny low lanterns on the glass rail posts (36), dim enough to stay well below the lava.
Pools behind alternate benches at the north wall; dark gaps between.

dressing.why: Rail 1.3 m in front of the hot glass (36 draws a railing along the glass).
Rock only at the north wall and ends; nothing between the benches and the glass.
Low-frequency 'heartbeat' (lookbook): audio emitters hidden in the north wall at both ends.

mood.palette: orange lava, bronze frames, near-black timber, very dim amber accents
mood.mist: None; heat shimmer on the glass.

waivers.reason: Benches sit on a 15 m rhythm (every other glass bay) on purpose; the bays are regular.
